To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and built two high power amplifiers with saturated output powers of 1-Watt, 4-Watt, and 36dBm, respectively, using standard low-cost plastic QFNs and that these amplifiers are compatible with standard SMT assembly processes.

we developed a new class of low-cost Ka-band high power amplifiers that produce +30dBm CW saturated output with 26% power added efficiency and +35 dBm saturated output power with 23% PAE in QFNs that are 4×4 mm2 and 5×5 mm2 respectively.
the new QFN packaged high power amplifires operating at Ka-band are the first of their kind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low-cost high power Ka-band packaged amplifies.
the design, fabrication and testing of high performance low-cost Ka-Band high-power packaged amplifiers.
the design and performance characterization of low-cost high power packaged amplifiers for commercial and military applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented packaged amplifiers have demonstrated the highest output power levels for their respective package sizes.
the presented packaged amplifiers are the smallest, lowest cost, and highest output power Ka-Band amplifiers available today.
these amplifiers represent a new class of high power packaged amplifiers that are fully compatible with SMD assembly techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully designed high power Ka-band amplifiers with low-cost standard off-the-shelve QFNs and conventional SMD assembly process.
these amplifiers demonstrate that the QFN packaging is a viable and cost-effective packaging solution for high power Ka-band amplifiers.

we have demonstrated a low-cost and high power Ka-band packaged amplifier that has a saturated output power of 1-Watt with PAE of at least 26% in a 4×4 mm2 package, and 4-Watts with PAE of more than 23% in a 5×5 mm2 package, with small signal gain from about 28 to 32 GHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QFN packaging technology is a viable option for high power amplifier applications at Ka-Band.
the new QFN packaged amplifiers can be used in many applications such as phased array antennas, active electronically scanned antennas (AESA) and satellite communication systems.
high power packaged amplifiers can be designed and produced at low cost using standard QFNs.
